q-122488.name: Question 1
q-122488.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=8$ and $r=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{8}{C}_{3} & =\frac{8!}{(8-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{8!}{5!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}3!} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 7\cdot 6}{6} \\  & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

q-1799.name: Question 2
q-1799.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

q-122557.name: Question 5
q-122557.problem: Consider the list of decimal digits from zero to nine that are multiples of three. If the order of the digits is not important, in how many ways can we choose two different digits from the list?
q-122557.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $4$ digits that are multiples of three ($0,3,6,9$), so $n=4.$ We want to select $2$ of those digits, so we have $r=2.$

Therefore, the number of choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{4}{C}_{2} & =\frac{4!}{(4-2)!\,2!} \\  & =\frac{4!}{2!2!} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{2!\cancel{2!}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{12}{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122550.name: Question 6
q-122550.problem: In a group of six dancers, if every possible pair dances together, what is the total number of dances?
q-122550.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $6$ people, so $n=6.$ We want to select $2$ of those people for each dance, so we have $r=2.$

Therefore, the number of dances is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{6}{C}_{2} & =\frac{6!}{(6-2)!\,2!} \\  & =\frac{6!}{4!2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}2!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{30}{2} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122550.html:
Question 6
?

In a group of six dancers, if every possible pair dances together, what is the total number of dances?

a
15
b
64
c
48
d
720
e
30
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The number of combinations of n objects taken r at a time is given by the formula nCr=n!(n−r)!r!.

There are 6 people, so n=6. We want to select 2 of those people for each dance, so we have r=2.

Therefore, the number of dances is

6C2=6!(6−2)!2!=6!4!2!=6⋅5⋅4!4!2!=6⋅52⋅1=302=15.

q-1781.name: Question 7
q-1781.problem: How many different ways can a group of four be made from a room of eighty people?
q-1781.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $80$ people, so $n=80.$ We want to select $4$ of those people for each group, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different potential groups of four is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{80}{C}_{4} & =\frac{80!}{(80-4)!\,4!} \\  & =\frac{80!}{76!4!} \\  & =\frac{80\cdot 79\cdot 78\cdot 77\cdot \cancel{76!}}{\cancel{76!}4!} \\  & =\frac{80\cdot 79\cdot 78\cdot 77}{4\cdot 3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{37\,957\,920}{24} \\  & =1\,581\,580.\end{aligned}
$$

q-5569.name: Question 8
q-5569.problem: Out of the ten contestants in an Olympic event, how many possible groups of $3$ medalists are there, regardless of which medal they win?
q-5569.worked_solution:
In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $10$ contestants, so $n=10.$ We want to select $3$ of those contestants for the medal positions, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different potential groups of medalists is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{C}_{3} & =\frac{10!}{(10-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{7!3!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}3!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{720}{6} \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$
